column1: # Line-count-pinned grandfather ledger for the 500-line file cap on tracked
# files under scripts/ (issue #8221), the scripts/ sibling of
# markdown-line-cap-grandfather.tsv: a closed list of the files that already
# exceeded the cap when the gate landed, so the gate lands green on today's tree
# and new or growing files fail immediately. These files are reported, not
# approved: each is debt to split by responsibility, and each row should be
# deleted by the change that brings its file to 500 lines or fewer.
# scripts/lib/tooling-line-cap-core.sh reads this file directly. Nothing
# regenerates it; edit it by hand, using
# `bash scripts/verify-tooling-line-cap.sh --pin <path>` to measure a row.
# "Closed list" is enforced: the gate compares this file against its committed
# baseline (TOOLING_LINE_CAP_BASE_REF, default origin/main) and accepts only
# REMOVING a row or LOWERING a pin. Adding a row or raising one is refused,
# because a change could otherwise add an over-cap file together with the row
# exempting it. If you are here to add a row for a new file, split the file
# instead.
# Columns (tab-separated): path<TAB>line_count
#   path       - repo-root-relative path of the file.
#   line_count - the file's exact line count (awk NR) when it was pinned.
# The pin is checked as `live <= line_count`. A file that grows past it fails.
# A file below it passes with a NOTE asking for a re-pin. A row is STALE, and
# the gate hard-fails on it, once its file no longer exists or is at or under
# 500 lines; the list only shrinks.
